question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


The brightest stars / can be 30,000 times / most luminous / than the Sun
options: most luminous
can be 30,000 times
than the Sun
The brightest stars
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "most luminous"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence requires comparative degree as it compares two entities (stars and Sun).
☛ "Most luminous" is a superlative degree used when comparing three or more things, which is incorrect here.
☛ The correct form should be "more luminous" since only two entities are being compared.
☛ "Than" is always paired with comparative degree (er/more), not superlative degree (est/most).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Degree: Used to compare two things. Example: faster, more intelligent.
☛ Superlative Degree: Used to compare three or more things (highest degree). Example: fastest, most intelligent.
☛ "Than" is strictly followed by comparative adjectives/adverbs.
☛ Rule: Positive → Comparative → Superlative (Example: tall → taller → tallest).

Example:
Incorrect - She is the most taller girl in class.
Correct - She is the tallest girl in class.

☛ "most luminous" superlative degree है जो तब प्रयोग होता है जब तीन या अधिक चीजों में से किसी एक को सर्वोत्तम बताया जाता है।
☛ यहाँ "more luminous" का प्रयोग सही होगा क्योंकि केवल दो चीजों (stars और Sun) की तुलना हो रही है।
☛ "than" के साथ हमेशा comparative degree (er/more) का प्रयोग होता है, superlative degree (est/most) का नहीं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Degree: दो चीजों की तुलना करने के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है। उदाहरण: bigger, more beautiful।
☛ Superlative Degree: तीन या अधिक चीजों में सर्वोत्तम बताने के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है। उदाहरण: biggest, most beautiful।
☛ "Than" हमेशा comparative degree के साथ आता है।
☛ नियम: Positive → Comparative → Superlative (उदाहरण: bright → brighter → brightest)।

Example:
Incorrect - This is the most better option.
Correct - This is the better option.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Uttar Pradesh / accounts for about 16 per cent / of the / country population.
options: accounts for about 16 per cent
of the
Uttar Pradesh
country population
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "country population"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "country population" is incorrect because it lacks the possessive form.
☛ Population is a noun belonging to the country, so it should be written as "country's population" with an apostrophe ('s).
☛ This is a common error-spotting question in competitive exams as students often miss the possessive form.
☛ Uttar Pradesh accounts for about 16 per cent of the country population. is wrong, while Uttar Pradesh accounts for about 16 per cent of the country's population. is correct.

Grammar Rules:
☛ The possessive case is used to show ownership or relationship.
☛ Singular nouns take 's (e.g., Rohan's book), while plural nouns take only an apostrophe (') (e.g., students' marks).
☛ Country is a singular noun, so country's is the correct form.

Example:
Incorrect - The team performance was poor.
Correct - The team's performance was poor.

☛ Population एक noun है जो country से संबंधित है, इसलिए apostrophe ('s) का प्रयोग करके "country's population" लिखा जाना चाहिए।
☛ यह error spotting प्रतियोगी परीक्षाओं में अक्सर पूछा जाता है क्योंकि छात्र possessive form को नजरअंदाज कर देते हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Possessive Case का प्रयोग ownership या relationship दिखाने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ Singular nouns के साथ 's लगता है (जैसे Rohan's book), जबकि plural nouns के साथ केवल apostrophe (') लगता है (जैसे students' marks).
☛ Country एक singular noun है, इसलिए country's सही रूप है।

Example:
Incorrect - The team performance was poor.
Correct - The team's performance was poor.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.


Time and technology are two important factor that change substances into resources.
options: factor that
two important
resources
Time and technology
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "factor that"

Explanation:
☛ The phrase "factor that" is incorrect because it does not match the plural form required by the sentence.
☛ The sentence begins with "Time and technology are", which indicates a plural subject.
☛ Therefore, "factor" should be replaced with "factors" to maintain subject-verb agreement.
☛ The word "that" is correctly used as a relative pronoun to provide additional information about the "factors".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: When the subject is plural, the verb must also be plural. Example: "The dogs bark loudly."
☛ Relative Pronoun: Words like "that", "which", or "who" add details about the preceding noun.
☛ Countable Nouns: Nouns that can be counted must be in plural form if the subject is plural.

Example:
Incorrect - Time and technology are two important factor that change substances into resources.
Correct - Time and technology are two important factors that change substances into resources. --
question_hi:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.


Time and technology are two important factor that change substances into resources.
options_hi: factor that
two important
resources
Time and technology
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "factor that"

Explanation:
☛ दिए गए वाक्य में "factor that" गलत है क्योंकि यहाँ बहुवचन (plural) का उपयोग होना चाहिए।
☛ वाक्य के शुरुआत में "Time and technology are" का प्रयोग हुआ है, जो बहुवचन (plural) को दर्शाता है।
☛ इसलिए, "factor" के बजाय "factors" का उपयोग होना चाहिए ताकि यह subject-verb agreement के नियम का पालन कर सके।
☛ "that" का प्रयोग सही है क्योंकि यह एक relative pronoun है जो "factors" के बारे में जानकारी देता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: जब subject plural होता है, तो verb भी plural होनी चाहिए। उदाहरण: "The books are on the table."
☛ Relative Pronoun: "that", "which", या "who" जैसे शब्द पहले आए noun के बारे में अतिरिक्त जानकारी देते हैं।
☛ Countable Nouns: जिन nouns को गिना जा सकता है, उनका plural form होना चाहिए यदि subject plural है।

Example:
Incorrect - Time and technology are two important factor that change substances into resources.
Correct - Time and technology are two important factors that change substances into resources.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


He had begun to dig / diligent along the / low tideline and had / captured two clams.
options: He had begun to dig
diligent along the
captured two clams
low tideline and had
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "diligent along the"

Explanation:
☛ The segment diligent along the contains a grammatical error.
☛ Diligent is an adjective, but an adverb is required here to modify the verb dig.
☛ The correct word should be diligently, which properly describes the action of digging.
☛ Adverbs are typically formed by adding "-ly" to adjectives (e.g., quick → quickly, happy → happily).
☛ This error highlights the misuse of Parts of Speech and Modifiers, a common topic in exams.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjective vs. Adverb: Adjectives modify nouns/pronouns, while adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
☛ -ly Rule: Most adverbs are formed by adding "-ly" to adjectives (e.g., slow → slowly).
☛ Verb Modification: Always use an adverb to describe a verb (e.g., She speaks fluently).

Example:
Incorrect - He works diligent.
Correct - He works diligently.

☛ Diligent एक adjective (विशेषण) है, जबकि यहाँ adverb (क्रिया-विशेषण) की आवश्यकता है क्योंकि यह dig (क्रिया) को modify कर रहा है।
☛ सही शब्द diligently होना चाहिए, जो क्रिया को सही ढंग से describe करेगा।
☛ Adverbs आमतौर पर adjectives से "-ly" जोड़कर बनाए जाते हैं (जैसे: quick → quickly, happy → happily)।
☛ यह त्रुटि Parts of Speech (शब्द-भेद) और Modifiers (विशेषक) के गलत उपयोग को दर्शाती है, जो परीक्षा में अक्सर पूछा जाता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjective vs. Adverb: Adjectives (विशेषण) संज्ञा/सर्वनाम को modify करते हैं, जबकि Adverbs (क्रिया-विशेषण) क्रिया, adjective या दूसरे adverb को modify करते हैं।
☛ -ly Rule: अधिकांश adverbs, adjectives के अंत में "-ly" जोड़कर बनते हैं (उदाहरण: slow → slowly).
☛ Verb Modification: जब किसी क्रिया की विशेषता बतानी हो, तो adverb का प्रयोग करें (उदाहरण: She speaks fluently).

Example:
Incorrect - He works diligent.
Correct - He works diligently.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


The earthy / fragrance of soil / after a first rain / is always refreshing.
options: The earthy
fragrance of soil
after a first rain
is always refreshing
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "after a first rain"

Explanation:
☛ Error in segment: The phrase "after a first rain" incorrectly uses the indefinite article "a".
☛ Rule: With ordinal numbers like "first," we use the definite article "the" to specify a particular instance (e.g., "the first rain of the season").
☛ Correct Structure: "after the first rain" (refers to a specific, known event).
☛ Exam Tip: In error-spotting, always check if ordinal numbers are paired with "the" instead of "a/an".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Ordinal Numbers + Articles: Use "the" before ordinals (e.g., the third attempt, the tenth page).
☛ Exception: If the ordinal is part of a title or general category, "a/an" may be used (e.g., a second chance).

Example:
Incorrect - He got a first rank in the exam.
Correct - He got the first rank in the exam.

Explanation:

☛ Rule: "first" एक ordinal number (क्रमसूचक संख्या) है जिसके साथ "the" article का use होता है, न कि "a/an"।
☛ Correct Structure: "the first rain" (विशिष्ट घटना को दर्शाने के लिए)
☛ Significance: Competitive exams में articles और ordinal numbers का combination अक्सर गलत होता है।

Example:
Incorrect - She won a first prize.
Correct - She won the first prize.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Human being are / the producers and the / consumers of Earth’s / resources.
options: resources
Human being are
consumers of Earth’s
the producers and the
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "Human being are"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "Human being are" because "Human being" is a singular noun while "are" is a plural verb.
☛ The correct plural form of "Human being" is "Human beings", which agrees with the plural verb "are".
☛ As per Subject-Verb Agreement rules, a singular subject must take a singular verb, and a plural subject must take a plural verb.
☛ Changing "being" to "beings" will make the sentence grammatically accurate.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: Use singular verb (is) with singular subject (e.g., Human being) and plural verb (are) with plural subject (e.g., Human beings).
☛ Countable Nouns: "Being" is countable, so add "s" for plural (beings).
☛ Error Spotting: Competitive exams often test Singular/Plural and Verb Agreement errors.

Example:
Incorrect - Human being are responsible for pollution.
Correct - Human beings are responsible for pollution.

☛ "Human being" का सही plural form "Human beings" होगा, जिसके साथ "are" का प्रयोग सही होगा।
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement के नियम के अनुसार, singular subject के साथ singular verb और plural subject के साथ plural verb का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
☛ यहाँ "being" को "beings" में बदलने से वाक्य grammatically correct हो जाएगा।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular subject (जैसे Human being) के साथ singular verb (is) और plural subject (जैसे Human beings) के साथ plural verb (are) का प्रयोग करें।
☛ Countable Nouns: "Being" एक countable noun है, इसलिए plural बनाने के लिए "s" जोड़ें (beings).
☛ Error Spotting: Competitive exams में अक्सर Singular/Plural और Verb Agreement से related errors पूछे जाते हैं।

Example:
Incorrect - Human being are responsible for pollution.
Correct - Human beings are responsible for pollution.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Most of the / freshwater lake in India / are in the / Himalayan region.
options: are in the
freshwater lake in India
Most of the
Himalayan region
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "freshwater lake in India"

Explanation:
☛ The segment 'freshwater lake in India' contains a grammatical error.
☛ 'Most of the' requires a plural noun, but 'lake' is singular.
☛ The correct phrase should be 'freshwater lakes in India' to match the plural verb 'are'.
☛ This follows the Subject-Verb Agreement rule where both subject and verb must be plural.
☛ Quantifiers like most/some always take plural nouns.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Phrases like Most of the/Some of the must be followed by plural nouns.
☛ Collective nouns (e.g., team) are singular, but here individual items (lakes) are referred to.
☛ In error spotting, focus on noun number and verb consistency.

Example:
Incorrect - Most of the book is torn. (if referring to pages)
Correct - Most of the books are torn.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


To descend a cragged / mountain, however, was most/ difficult and dangerous / than to ascend it.
options: than to ascend it
To descend a cragged
mountain however was most
difficult and dangerous
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "mountain however was most"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the segment 'mountain however was most'.
☛ 'most' is incorrect here because when comparing two things, 'more' (comparative degree) should be used instead of 'most' (superlative degree).
☛ 'than' requires 'more', e.g., "more difficult than".
☛ The correct phrase should be: "mountain however was more".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Degree: Use '-er' or 'more' when comparing two things (e.g., "taller than", "more beautiful than").
☛ Superlative Degree: Use '-est' or 'most' when comparing three or more things (e.g., "the tallest", "the most beautiful").
☛ 'Than' always follows the comparative degree.

Example:
Incorrect - "This book is most interesting than that."
Correct - "This book is more interesting than that."

solution_hi:

☛ 'most' का प्रयोग यहाँ गलत है क्योंकि जब दो चीजों की तुलना की जाती है, तो 'more' (तुलनात्मक डिग्री) का प्रयोग होना चाहिए, न कि 'most' (उत्तम डिग्री) का।
☛ 'than' के साथ 'more' का प्रयोग होता है, जैसे: "more difficult than"।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative Degree: जब दो चीजों की तुलना की जाती है, तो '-er' या 'more' का प्रयोग करें (उदा. "taller than", "more beautiful than").
☛ Superlative Degree: जब तीन या अधिक चीजों की तुलना की जाती है, तो '-est' या 'most' का प्रयोग करें (उदा. "the tallest", "the most beautiful").

Example:

Correct - "This book is more interesting than that."

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Scholars have / studied the lives of / present-day farmer’s / who practice agriculture.
options: Scholars have
who practice agriculture
studied the lives of
present-day farmer’s
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "present-day farmer’s"

Explanation:
☛ Error: The error lies in "present-day farmer’s" due to incorrect use of the possessive case.
☛ Rule: Apostrophe (') is used only for possession or contraction. Here, "farmer" is a plural noun (referring to multiple farmers), not a possessive form.
☛ Correct Form: "present-day farmers" (without apostrophe) as it’s a simple plural, not possessive.
☛ Exam Tip: If the sentence already uses "of" (e.g., "lives of"), an apostrophe is redundant.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Apostrophe Rules:
- Singular Possessive: farmer’s land (one farmer’s land).
- Plural Possessive: farmers’ land (multiple farmers’ land).

But this immortality / will have purchased / at the price of / his immortal part.
options: will have purchased
But this immortality
his immortal part
at the price of
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "will have purchased"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "will have purchased" because it is a Passive Voice construction, which requires the use of "be" verb.
☛ The correct structure should be: "will have been purchased" since the object (immortality) is being purchased, not purchasing itself.
☛ "At the price of" and "his immortal part" are correct as they form proper Prepositional Phrase and Noun Phrase.
☛ "But this immortality" is also correct as it is the Subject of the sentence with no error.

Grammar Rules:
☛ In Future Perfect Tense, Passive Voice is formed using "will have been + V3".
☛ In Passive Voice, the Object of Active Voice becomes the Subject, and the Verb takes its third form (V3).
☛ Incorrect: The book will have written by him.
Correct: The book will have been written by him.

options: We've got to have

human intelligence
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "including much strong"

Explanation:
☛ Error: The phrase "including much strong" is incorrect because "much" is used with uncountable nouns, while "strong" is an adjective that cannot be modified by "much".
☛ Correct Usage: To show comparison, "much stronger" should be used as the sentence includes "than before", which demands a comparative degree.
☛ Rule: "Much" can modify comparative adjectives (e.g., much stronger), but not positive degree adjectives.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Much vs. Many: "Much" pairs with uncountable nouns (e.g., much effort), while "many" pairs with countable nouns (e.g., many mistakes).
☛ Comparative Adjectives: Always use comparative degree (e.g., smarter, taller) with "than".
☛ Adverb Use: "Much" can modify adverbs (e.g., much more efficiently) or comparative adjectives, not positive adjectives.

Example:
Incorrect - She is much happy.
Correct - She is much happier.

question:

Thunderstorms develop / in hot, humid, tropical areas / like India much to / frequently.
options: like India much to
in hot, humid, tropical areas
Thunderstorms develop
frequently
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "like India much to"

Explanation:
☛ Error: The segment "like India much to" is incorrect because "much to" is contextually inappropriate here.
☛ Correct Phrase: It should be "like India very much" or "like India a lot". "Much to" is typically used in phrases like "much to someone's surprise", not to indicate frequency.
☛ Context: The sentence means "Thunderstorms develop frequently in tropical areas like India." "Frequently" pairs with "very much" or "a lot", not "much to".
☛ Exam Tip: Note the difference between "much to" (for emotional reactions) and "very much" (for degree/quantity). Example: Much to her delight, he arrived early (correct) vs She likes India much to (incorrect).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adverb Usage: "Very much" or "a lot" are adverbs indicating degree/frequency, while "much to" is a prepositional phrase.
☛ Common Errors: Never substitute "much to" for "very much". Example: Incorrect: He travels much to → Correct: He travels a lot.
☛ Fixed Phrases: "Much to" is correct only in specific constructions like Much to my surprise, she agreed.

Example:
Incorrect - They celebrate festivals much to.
Correct - They celebrate festivals very much.

question:

options: A tiger’s skull

to

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "a lion"

Explanation:
☛ The segment a lion is incorrect because it lacks the possessive case ('s) required here.
☛ The sentence compares two things - A tiger's skull and a lion's skull. Without 's, the comparison becomes illogical.
☛ In comparative structures, both terms must maintain parallel grammatical forms. Here, skull should be compared with lion's skull, not just lion.
☛ The principle of parallelism is crucial in such comparative constructions in English.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Possessive Case: Use 's when a noun owns or is associated with something (John's pen, cat's paw).
☛ Comparative Structures: With similar to, different from, same as etc., both compared elements must have matching structures.
☛ Parallel Construction: When comparing two things, maintain identical grammatical forms (Her dress is prettier than mine - not than me).

Example:
Incorrect - Your car is faster than Ramesh.
Correct - Your car is faster than Ramesh's.

In the primitive / oceans, / life begins / nearly 3.5 billion years ago.
options_hi: nearly 3.5 billion years ago
oceans
life begins
In the primitive
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "life begins"

Explanation:
☛ वाक्य में एक grammatical error है "life begins" सेक्शन में।
☛ वाक्य में समय "nearly 3.5 billion years ago" दिया गया है जो past tense (भूतकाल) को दर्शाता है।
☛ "life begins" present tense (वर्तमान काल) में है जो past time reference के साथ मेल नहीं खाता।
☛ सही form "life began" (past simple tense) होनी चाहिए क्योंकि यह एक past event को describe कर रहा है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Tense consistency (काल संगति) का नियम: वाक्य में समय के सन्दर्भ और verb के tense में सामंजस्य होना चाहिए।
☛ Past time expressions (जैसे 'ago', 'yesterday', 'last year') के साथ हमेशा past tense का प्रयोग होता है।
☛ Present simple tense का प्रयोग general truths (सामान्य सत्य) या habitual actions (आदतन कार्य) के लिए होता है, past events के लिए नहीं।

Example:
Incorrect - Life begins nearly 3.5 billion years ago.
Correct - Life began nearly 3.5 billion years ago.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Continuous heavy / rainfall may / further worse / the flood situation.
options: rainfall may
the flood situation
further worse
Continuous heavy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "further worse"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "further worse" is incorrect because "worse" is a comparative adjective and cannot be used with "further".
☛ "Further" is used as an adverb, indicating additional deterioration, but pairing it with an adjective ("worse") is grammatically wrong.
☛ The correct form is "worsen", a verb meaning "to make or become worse."
☛ Continuous heavy rainfall may further worsen the flood situation. — This is the correct sentence.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Comparative adjectives (e.g., worse, better) compare two things, but for indicating action, a verb form must be used.
☛ "Further" is an adverb meaning "to a greater extent," used to modify verbs, not adjectives.
☛ "Worsen" is a dynamic verb showing progression of deterioration, making it the right choice here.

Example:
Incorrect - The conflict may further worse.
Correct - The conflict may worsen further.

☛ "Further" का प्रयोग adverb के रूप में किया जाता है, जो कि पहले से मौजूद स्थिति को और बिगाड़ने की ओर इशारा करता है, लेकिन "worse" के साथ यह grammatically incorrect है।
☛ सही प्रयोग "worsen" होगा, जो कि एक verb है और यह बताता है कि बाढ़ की स्थिति और खराब होगी।

Grammar Rules:

☛ "Further" एक adverb है जिसका अर्थ है "और अधिक," और यह किसी क्रिया को modify करने के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है, न कि adjective को।
☛ "Worsen" एक dynamic verb है जो किसी स्थिति के और खराब होने का संकेत देता है, इसलिए यहाँ इसका प्रयोग सही है।

Example:
Incorrect - The situation may further worse.
Correct - The situation may worsen further.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Concern above rising pollution / led to the / formulation of / various action plans.
options: formulation of
Concern above rising pollution
various action plans
led to the
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "Concern above rising pollution"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in 'Concern above rising pollution' because 'above' is incorrectly used here.
☛ The correct prepositions to use with 'concern' are 'about' or 'over', as they convey the meaning of 'regarding'.
☛ 'Above' refers to physical position (e.g., The clock is above the door), while 'about'/'over' refers to abstract relations (e.g., Concern about climate change).
☛ The corrected sentence would be: "Concern about/over rising pollution led to the formulation of various action plans."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Prepositions must match the context. 'Above' indicates physical placement, whereas 'about'/'over' indicate abstract connections.
☛ Words like 'concern' pair with 'about'/'over', not 'above'.
☛ Competitive exams often test such prepositional errors to assess grammatical accuracy.

Example:
Incorrect - Concern above rising pollution
Correct - Concern about/over rising pollution

-----------------

☛ Concern जैसे शब्दों के साथ 'about'/'over' का प्रयोग होता है, न कि 'above'।

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.


Seeds of mustard plants give us oil, and the leave are used as a vegetable.
options: Seeds of
give us oil
leave are used
as a vegetable
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "leave are used"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in the part "leave are used".
☛ Since the sentence refers to the leaves (plural) of mustard plants used as a vegetable, the correct plural form should be "leaves", not "leave" (singular).
☛ "Leave" is singular and incorrect here because multiple leaves are used, making the verb "are" correct, but the noun must agree in number.
☛ This error is related to Subject-Verb Agreement and pluralization rules.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Singular & Plural Nouns: Some nouns have irregular plural forms, e.g., leaf → leaves, mouse → mice.
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject takes a singular verb, while a plural subject takes a plural verb.
☛ Common Mistakes: Always check if the noun represents one (singular) or many (plural) items.

Example:
Incorrect - The ox are heavy.
Correct - The oxen are heavy.

☛ Common Irregular Plurals: Child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth याद रखें।

Example:
Incorrect - The leave is green.
Correct - The leaves are green.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.


We are all aware that our environment are not what it used to be.
options: aware that our
We are all
environment are not
What it used to be
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "environment are not"

Explanation:
☛ Here, 'environment' is a singular noun, meaning 'the natural world'.
☛ Using the plural verb 'are' with a singular noun is incorrect. It should be replaced with 'is'.
☛ The sentence violates the Subject-Verb Agreement rule, which states that a singular subject takes a singular verb, and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
☛ Hence, "environment are not" is incorrect and should be "environment is not".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement Rule:
- A singular subject takes a singular verb. (Example: The cat meows softly.)
- A plural subject takes a plural verb. (Example: The cats meow softly.)
☛ Collective nouns like 'team', 'family', 'environment' are generally treated as singular.

Example:
Incorrect - The committee are discussing the issue.
Correct - The committee is discussing the issue.

☛ Singular noun के साथ plural verb 'are' का प्रयोग गलत है। इसकी जगह 'is' का प्रयोग होना चाहिए था।
☛ यहाँ वाक्य Subject-Verb Agreement के नियम का उल्लंघन करता है, जिसके अनुसार singular subject के साथ singular verb और plural subject के साथ plural verb आती है।

Grammar Rules:

- Singular subject (एकवचन कर्ता) के साथ singular verb (एकवचन क्रिया) आती है। (Example: The dog barks loudly.)
- Plural subject (बहुवचन कर्ता) के साथ plural verb (बहुवचन क्रिया) आती है। (Example: The dogs bark loudly.)
☛ Collective nouns (समूहवाचक संज्ञाएँ) जैसे 'team', 'family', 'environment', आमतौर पर singular मानी जाती हैं।

Example:

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


Scientists believe / that many animals have / a unique languages / of their own.
options: of their own
a unique languages
Scientists believe
that many animals have
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "a unique languages"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "a unique languages" because "unique" is a singular adjective that modifies a singular noun.
☛ "Languages" is plural and does not agree with "unique".
☛ Correct structure should be: "a unique language" (singular) or "unique languages" (plural, but without the article "a").
☛ Article "a" is only used with singular, countable nouns.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Indefinite articles (a/an) are used only with singular countable nouns. Example: a pen, an umbrella.
☛ Adjective-noun agreement is essential. Adjectives like unique denoting inherent quality do not adjust for singular/plural nouns.
☛ Many is always followed by a plural noun. Example: many cars, many students.

Example:
Incorrect - He has a creative ideas.
Correct - He has a creative idea.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.


If you plant a seed, / you will be noticed / that it takes some / time to grow.
options: you will be noticed
that it takes some
If you plant a seed
time to grow
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "you will be noticed"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "you will be noticed" contains a grammatical error because it does not fit the context of the sentence.
☛ The intended meaning is: "If you plant a seed, you will notice that it takes some time to grow."
☛ "Noticed" is incorrect here as it is in passive voice, while active voice ("you will notice") should be used.
☛ Passive voice is used when the subject receives the action, but here the subject (you) is performing the action (notice).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Active Voice: The subject performs the action. Example: "She writes a letter."
☛ Passive Voice: The subject receives the action. Example: "A letter is written by her."
☛ In this sentence, active voice is correct because the subject (you) is performing the action (notice).

Example:
Incorrect - If you study, you will be given knowledge.
Correct - If you study, you will gain knowledge.

Grammar Rules:

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.


The jute plant is usual harvested when it is at the flowering stage.
options: is usual harvested
The jute plant
at the flowering stage
when it is
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "is usual harvested"

Explanation:
☛ Error: The phrase "is usual harvested" is grammatically incorrect because "usual" is an adjective, but it is incorrectly modifying the verb "harvested."
☛ Rule: Adverbs (e.g., "usually") modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, while adjectives (e.g., "usual") only describe nouns or pronouns.
☛ Correct Form: It should be "is usually harvested" since the adverb "usually" correctly modifies the verb "harvested."
☛ Exam Tip: In error spotting, adjective/adverb confusion is a frequent mistake. Remember: Adverb = Verb + ly (unless irregular).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjective vs. Adverb: Adjectives (usual, happy) describe nouns, while adverbs (usually, happily) modify verbs/adjectives.
☛ Position: Adverbs typically appear after the main verb or between auxiliary verbs (is, has) and the main verb.
☛ Examples:
Incorrect - He speaks loud.
Correct - He speaks loudly. --

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.


Neither she not I am going to take part in the debate competition.
options: Neither she not I
am going to take part
in the debate competition
No error
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "Neither she not I"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "Neither she not I".
☛ The correct correlative conjunction is "Neither...nor", used to connect two negative alternatives.
☛ Here, "not" is incorrectly used instead of "nor".
☛ According to Subject-Verb Agreement, when two subjects are connected by "Neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearest subject. Here, "am" is correct as it agrees with "I".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Neither...nor is used to join two negative options.
☛ If the subjects differ in number (singular/plural), the verb agrees with the nearest subject.
☛ Example: Neither he nor his friends are coming. (Here, "friends" is plural, so "are" is correct.)

Example:
Incorrect - Neither she not I am going to take part in the debate competition.
Correct - Neither she nor I am going to take part in the debate competition.

☛ "Neither...nor" एक सही संयोजक (conjunction) है जो दो विकल्पों को जोड़ने के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛ यहाँ "not" का प्रयोग गलत है, इसे "nor" से बदलना चाहिए।
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement के अनुसार, यदि दो subjects "Neither...nor" से जुड़े हों, तो verb निकटतम subject के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ verb "am" सही है क्योंकि यह "I" के साथ agree करती है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Neither...nor का प्रयोग दो नकारात्मक विकल्पों को जोड़ने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ यदि subjects अलग-अलग numbers (एकवचन/बहुवचन) में हों, तो verb निकटतम subject के अनुसार होती है।
☛ Example: Neither he nor his friends are coming. (यहाँ "friends" बहुवचन है, इसलिए "are" सही है।)

Example:
Incorrect - Neither she not I am going to take part in the debate competition.
Correct - Neither she nor I am going to take part in the debate competition.
